description: Detect prompt injection, jailbreaks, secrets, PII, and unsafe AI instructions in n8n workflows

hints.message: Flagged items leave through the second output. Connect it to a response or stop step, or leave it unconnected to drop them — but do not connect it back into your main path.
Passport token fields are masked in the editor. Keep Include Raw API Response off for lifecycle workflows unless debugging; token-shaped keys in raw responses are redacted.
On Threat is set to Continue, so nothing is ever stopped and the Flagged output stays empty. Use Block or Redact for real enforcement.
No Session ID set. Each message will be judged on its own, so an attack spread across several turns can pass one harmless-looking message at a time. Add one under Options.
Topic Handling is set to Advisory, so your Allowed Semantic Topics only annotate the result. If ordinary questions about these topics are being blocked, switch it to Trust My Topics under Options.

Always Allow skips detection completely for messages that match one of your lines exactly. Nothing about them is scanned, and the result is marked bypassed: ALWAYS_ALLOW. Keep the list to the questions you are certain about.

Sensitivity is Lenient: borderline findings are reported but not enforced, so expect fewer stops and more items on Safe. Live secrets and clear injection or jailbreak attempts are still stopped at every level.

Local mode can only compare the output against Protected Sources whose text is supplied inline, because resolving a bare source ID needs the cloud fingerprint store. Sources given by ID alone are reported as unresolved, never as clean.

Reduced protection: Local is a pattern-only first filter (measured prompt-injection recall is about 18% on the published out-of-distribution corpus). It has no ML tier, cross-turn tracking, reputation, or passport enforcement. Use Auto for cloud-first production protection.
Identity and passport lifecycle operations use server-side state. They require a SoterAI API Key (x-api-key) and never fall back to Local.
Redaction branching is active. Clean items leave through Clean (output 1) and items with redacted PII/secrets leave through Redacted (output 2).

On Threat is set to Block, but Also Enforce On Sensitive Data is off under Options. Secrets and personal data will be redacted and continue through Safe. Turn it on under Options if you want Block to stop them.
Custom JSON Only starts from an empty policy, so this agent would be granted nothing. Add Policy Overrides (JSON) under Options.

properties.displayName: This operation enforces. On Threat decides what happens to anything flagged, and flagged items leave through the Flagged output instead of the main path.
properties.name: enforcingNotice

properties.displayName: Reports risk without blocking, but it still routes: anything it flags leaves through Flagged. Connect that output to stop the item, or leave it unconnected to drop it.
properties.name: reportOnlyNotice

properties.displayName: Never blocks and never stops an item. The cleaned copy arrives as {{ $json.outputText }} on the single output; the text you pass in is not modified in place.
properties.name: redactNotice

properties.displayName: The workflow JSON is analysed in-process and never sent to SoterAI. Static review only — it never executes the workflow or resolves a credential.
properties.name: auditNotice

properties.displayName: Step 1 of 5: Register the agent once, then pass {{ $json.agentIdentityId }} to Issue Access Pass.
properties.name: enrollIdentityNotice

properties.displayName: Step 2 of 5: Issue a short-lived access pass for one session. Pass sessionId and passportToken by expression; never paste the token into workflow JSON.
properties.name: issuePassportNotice

properties.displayName: Step 3 of 5: Validate the session and token. Session ID and Passport Token auto-pick from incoming item if left empty. Tool Name and Tool Action test authorization for a specific call.
properties.name: validatePassportNotice

properties.displayName: Step 4 of 5: Put this immediately before the real tool. ALLOW leaves through Safe; blocked, invalid, or approval-required calls leave through Flagged.
properties.name: toolCallNotice

properties.displayName: Step 5 of 5: Revoke by Session ID or Access Pass ID when the task ends. Successful revocation returns PASSPORT_REVOKED on Safe.
properties.name: revokePassportNotice

properties.name: sensitivity

options.name: Balanced (Default)
options.description: Stop anything the engine judges unsafe. Same behaviour as every previous version of this node.

options.name: Lenient (Fewest Blocks)
options.description: Stop only confident, high-risk verdicts. Borderline findings are reported and the message continues — best for public helpdesks where a wrong block costs a customer.

options.name: Strict (Most Blocks)
options.description: Also act on findings Balanced would only report. Expect more false positives.

properties.hint: Sets HOW MUCH gets flagged. 'On Threat' sets WHAT HAPPENS. On Output Guard under Lenient, detected secrets are redacted into safeText and outputText rather than hard-blocked, letting the assistant response continue.
properties.description: How much risk is enough to act on. Live secrets and clear attacks are always acted on whatever this is set to — `sensitivity.effect` on the result says when the dial was overruled, and why.

properties.name: securityContext
properties.description: Optional extra layers to check alongside the prompt and response. Add only the ones your workflow actually has — each is independent.

properties.name: userMessages
properties.description: Your own wording for the customer-facing message, replacing the built-in English

options.name: allowed
options.placeholder: Thanks! Checking that for you now.
options.description: Shown when the message passed

options.name: blocked
options.placeholder: Sorry, I can't help with that one. Please rephrase it and try again.
options.description: The custom block message. Used for any stopped message with no more specific reply set below, so on its own it replaces every block message the node produces.

options.name: offTopic
options.placeholder: I can only help with orders, billing and returns.
options.description: Shown when Topic Handling stopped a message for being out of scope. Nothing was judged dangerous.

options.name: promptInjection
options.placeholder: I can only help with normal support questions.
options.description: Shown for prompt injection, jailbreak, or system-prompt extraction attempts

options.name: redacted
options.placeholder: I've removed some private details so we can continue safely.
options.description: Shown when sensitive data was removed and the message continued

options.name: needsRephrase
options.placeholder: Could you rewrite that without the private details?
options.description: Shown when the verdict was to ask for a safer version rather than to stop outright

options.name: sensitiveData
options.placeholder: Please don't share passwords or card numbers here.
options.description: Shown when a secret, card number, or personal identifier was the reason

options.name: allowedTopics
options.hint: Optional. Comma-separated. Topic Handling does nothing while this is empty.
options.description: Subjects this assistant handles, comma-separated. Leave empty for no topic scope.

options.name: enforceOnSensitiveData
options.hint: Off: a secret or personal detail is always removed and the item continues, whatever On Threat says. On: On Threat decides — Block stops the item and routes it to Flagged. The cleaned text is used either way; this never passes an unredacted secret through.
options.description: Whether On Threat also acts on an item whose only finding is a secret or personal data

options.name: alwaysAllow
options.placeholder:
where is my order?
how do I reset my password?
options.hint: One message per line. Matched on the WHOLE message, ignoring case and a trailing '?'
options.description: Whole messages that skip detection entirely. Whole-message match, not keywords.

options.name: detectionEngine
Auto — Cloud, Local Fallback (Recommended)
options.description: Use the cloud, and fall back to the local engine only when the cloud cannot be reached. No item is left unchecked. The right default for almost everyone.

options.name: Cloud Only
options.description: Full detection through the SoterAI API — ML tier, cross-turn tracking, reputation, incident history — and fail the item on an outage rather than fall back. Strongest, but needs a reachable API.

options.name: Local Only (No API Key, No Network)
options.description: Run the bundled rule engine inside n8n. Nothing leaves your instance and no credential is needed. Pattern-based, so weaker than Cloud.
Where detection runs. Auto (cloud with local fallback) suits almost everyone.

options.name: ignoredEntities
National ID (EU: BSN, DNI/NIE, Codice Fiscale)

options.hint: Leave empty to redact everything. Credentials — API keys, private keys, tokens — can never be ignored
options.description: Identifier types to leave unredacted. Credentials can never be ignored.

options.name: ignoredWords
options.hint: One per line, case-insensitive. Never applies to credentials — a line containing an API key, token, or private key is refused, not kept. Values survive in Local mode; in Cloud mode the server may redact them before the node sees them.
options.description: Literal words or phrases to leave unredacted wherever they appear

options.name: includeRawResponse
options.description: Whether to attach the full API response as rawResponse. It is recursively sanitized first, but turning it off keeps run data smaller on high-volume workflows.

options.name: batchConcurrency
options.description: How many input items to check at the same time. The default of 1 is sequential, so a hundred items are a hundred requests one after another, not a burst. Raising it is the single biggest speed win on large batches; a 429 is retried after the interval the API asks for either way. Order of the output items never changes.

options.name: metadata
options.hint: Optional. Extra fields for your own audit logs.
options.description: JSON object attached to the request for audit logging. Secrets and long strings are redacted before sending.

options.name: neverDowngradeToLocal
options.description: Whether to fail an item instead of answering it with the local engine when the cloud cannot be reached. For workflows under a compliance commitment that every message is checked by the full engine. With n8n's Continue On Fail set, failed items still leave through the Flagged output rather than Safe.

options.name: projectId
options.placeholder: Leave empty to use the credential's project
options.hint: Optional. Only needed when this node should report to a different project than the credential
options.description: SoterAI project ID, overriding the one set on the credential

options.name: requestTimeoutMs
options.description: How long to wait for each API call before giving up. In Auto mode a timeout is what triggers the local fallback.

options.name: reuseIdenticalItems
options.description: Whether two identical items in the same execution reuse one API call. The reused item is marked reusedResult so it is never mistaken for a second independent check.

options.name: sessionId
options.hint: Recommended. Keeps one conversation's messages together across turns.
options.description: Stable per-conversation ID. Without it each message is judged alone, so a slow multi-turn attack can pass one message at a time.

options.name: systemPromptContext
options.placeholder: You are a billing support assistant for an Indian e-commerce store
options.hint: Optional. Use it when the topic list is not specific enough — its words widen the topic vocabulary
options.description: Your assistant's role, used to judge whether a message is in scope

Advisory Only
options.description: Report whether the message was in scope and change nothing else

options.name: Stay on Topic
options.description: Also treat an out-of-scope message as something to act on. Reported as OFF_TOPIC, never as a threat.

options.name: Trust My Topics (Default)
options.description: Stop treating ordinary questions about your own topics as attacks. The usual fix for a helpdesk that blocks its own customers.

options.name: Trust My Topics and Stay on Topic
options.description: Both of the above: in-scope questions run freely, out-of-scope ones are acted on
